themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a historical average of 0.9 per week (357% increase, z-score: 2.46), suggesting either new unlicensed shops, operational issues at existing retailers, or a sudden enforcement wave in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
357% spike with z-score of 2.46 (high statistical significance)
Active ULURP at 350 Grand Concourse (FRESH market proposal) may signal retail activity concentration in district
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed cannabis shops proliferating in the neighborhood, and what enforcement response is underway?
What are residents complaining about—odor, loitering, noise, or operational violations at existing legal retailers?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Services Demand Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints surged to 13 two weeks ago versus a 2.6 weekly average (395% increase, z-score: 3.86—highest severity spike), indicating a sudden surge in encampments, visible homelessness, or unmet services in this district.
evidence: 13 complaints two weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average—highest z-score (3.86) in entire dataset
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'other services for the homeless' (Department of Homeless Services) in budget cycle, indicating chronic underfunding
No recent news coverage or community board meeting agendas provided, suggesting issue may be underreported
reporting_angles: What triggered the spike in homeless person assistance calls two weeks ago—new encampment, shelter closure, or seasonal migration?
How are DHS and local nonprofits responding, and what gaps exist in available shelter/services?
Interview residents and advocacy groups on ground conditions and what services are actually needed.

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise & Vehicle Disruption
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 11 last week (126% increase from 4.9 avg, z-score: 2.85) and vehicle noise spiked to 25 two weeks ago (153% increase from 9.9 avg, z-score: 2.47), suggesting new late-night commercial activity or unregulated vehicle operations in the district.
evidence: Noise - Commercial: 11 complaints last week vs. 4.9 weekly baseline (126% spike, z-score: 2.85)
Noise - Vehicle: 25 complaints two weeks ago vs. 9.9 weekly baseline (153% spike, z-score: 2.47)
Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints also up 96% last week (12 vs. 6.1 avg), suggesting possible disorder tied to commercial activity
reporting_angles: What new commercial establishments (bars, restaurants, venues, construction) opened or expanded recently in the district?
Are there venues operating without proper noise permits or late-night licenses, and what enforcement action is available?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Concerns Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.8 per week (300% increase, z-score: 2.71), suggesting possible foodborne illness cluster or contamination at local food service establishments.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 2.71)
No follow-up data provided on whether complaints were resolved or escalated to Health Department investigation
Active FRESH market proposal at 350 Grand Concourse under zoning review—potentially relevant to food retail in district
reporting_angles: Which food service establishments were cited, and what violations did DOHMH inspectors find?
Is there a foodborne illness cluster, or are these isolated incidents across different venues?

themes_detail.label: Street Obstruction & Access Issues
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints doubled last week to 4 versus a 1.4 weekly average (191% increase, z-score: 3.06), suggesting debris, blocked sidewalks, or parked vehicles compromising pedestrian access—aligns with perennial CB requests for street/building improvements.
evidence: 4 obstruction complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (191% spike, z-score: 3.06)
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'park, building, or access improvements' and capital projects, suggesting underlying maintenance backlog
429 DOB alteration filings in last 90 days (270 alterations, 107 new buildings) may correlate with construction debris and sidewalk blocking
reporting_angles: What types of obstructions are being reported—construction debris, illegally parked vehicles, or lack of maintenance?
Are DOB construction projects completing without proper site cleanup, and is enforcement adequate?
